# Vantage Telescope Handbook

## Mirror care

- The Vantage telescope's primary mirror is washed with distilled water and a drop of dish soap no more than once every 18 months, and never on a humid night. Dust is blown off with the rubber bulb in between, and the mirror cover goes back on within ten minutes of the last observer leaving, because dew forms quickly in the dome once the heating is off.
- The mirror cell has three support pads and three radial restraints, and the restraints are backed off by half a turn whenever the telescope is parked for more than a week. A mirror held too tightly goes astigmatic, which shows as a cross-shaped flare on bright stars, and the fault is easy to mistake for bad seeing until the stars are checked at several altitudes.
- Collimation is checked at the start of every observing session with the Cheshire eyepiece, and the secondary is only adjusted when the donut is off centre by more than a third of its width. Adjust in steps of an eighth of a turn and recheck after each, since the three screws fight each other and a large move on one overshoots the others.
- The dome's dehumidifier is switched on automatically when the humidity exceeds 62 percent and holds until it falls below 55. The humidity logger in the control room records both values every ten minutes, and the log is read on Monday mornings by whoever has the weekly duty so that a failing unit is noticed in days, not months.
- The focuser's rack is lubricated with a pea of lithium grease twice a year, in March and September, and the excess is wiped from the drawtube so that it does not creep onto the optics when the tube points down at the horizon during the winter observing programme.
